tip: The -alım ending makes a we-suggestion: buluşalım = let's meet. Adding mı turns it into a question, so buluşalım mı asks shall we.
Okuduğum means that I read: the -dığım ending on a verb builds a relative clause, so Okuduğum kitap = the book that I read.
The -erek ending means by doing something: dinleyerek = by listening, telling you how the falling asleep happens.
geldiği için means because it came: a verb plus -dığı için gives the reason, here why I missed the meeting.
kalkıp uses -ıp to chain verbs under one tense: geç kalkıp kahvaltı hazırlarız = we wake up late and make breakfast.
konuştukça uses -dıkça for the more, the more: konuştukça anlıyorum = the more I talk, the more I understand.
gitmek yerine means instead of going: an infinitive plus yerine expresses choosing one action over another.
dağıtılır is passive: the -ıl ending drops the doer, so it means letters are distributed with no mention of who does it.
oynardık means we used to play: the -rdık ending marks a repeated past habit, not a single event.
Ne yaparsam yapayım means whatever I do: the frame repeats the verb, yaparsam then yapayım, to say no matter what.
her gidişimde means every time I go: her plus the verbal noun gidiş with -imde marks each occasion something happens.
Turkish adds an apostrophe before a suffix on a proper name: Fatma'nın = Fatma's, keeping the name readable.
Her ne kadar with a later da means although: Her ne kadar yorgun olsam da = no matter how tired I am.
